A.explanation: Gives the correct powers $\text{kg m s}^{-3}$ but uses $^{\circ}\text{C}^{-1}$, and degree Celsius is not an SI base unit.

B.explanation: Rearranging gives $k = QL/[tA(T_1-T_2)]$ which simplifies to $\text{kg m s}^{-3}\text{K}^{-1}$ using joules, metres, seconds and kelvin.

C.explanation: Uses $\text{s}^{-1}$ instead of $\text{s}^{-3}$ and $^{\circ}\text{C}^{-1}$ instead of $\text{K}^{-1}$, so both the power and temperature unit are wrong.

D.explanation: Uses kelvin correctly but has $\text{m s}^{-1}$ instead of $\text{m s}^{-3}$, missing a factor of $\text{s}^{-2}$ from energy over time.

hints: Notice that $Q$ is thermal energy, so write its SI unit in joules and then in base units $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$.
Rearrange $Q/t = kA(T_1-T_2)/L$ to make $k$ the subject, so $k = QL/[tA(T_1-T_2)]$ with $L$ in $\text{m}$, $A$ in $\text{m}^2$ and $t$ in $\text{s}$.
Check the temperature difference $(T_1-T_2)$: SI base temperature is the kelvin $\text{K}$, not degree Celsius, and compare the powers of $\text{s}$ from $Q/t$.
walkthrough: Write down what each quantity contributes: $Q$ is energy in $\text{J}$, $L$ is length in $\text{m}$, $t$ is time in $\text{s}$, $A$ is area in $\text{m}^2$, and $(T_1-T_2)$ is temperature difference in $\text{K}$ for SI base units.
Rearrange the given relation for $k$: $Q/t = kA(T_1-T_2)/L$ gives $k = QL/[tA(T_1-T_2)]$.
Express energy $Q$ in base units: $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$ from work $force \times distance$.
Substitute all base units: $k$ has units $(\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2})(\text{m})/[(\text{s})(\text{m}^2)(\text{K})]$.
Simplify powers: numerator is $\text{kg m}^3 \text{s}^{-2}$ and denominator is $\text{m}^2 \text{s K}$, leaving $\text{kg m s}^{-3}\text{K}^{-1}$.

Degree Celsius cannot appear because the SI base unit for temperature is kelvin, and the $\text{s}^{-3}$ comes from $\text{s}^{-2}$ for energy plus one more $\text{s}^{-1}$ for dividing by time $t$. This is option B.
